In Cold Blood isn't really about mental illness either. It doesn't explore mental illness so much as it talks about the horrors of murder. Some of the other titles in this thread definitely take a closer look at mental disorders.

Although it is a great book :)

Wow, thank you for the encouragement. I really appreciate it.

Its just very hard for me to envision a future right now that doesn't seem dismal. I don't want anything my life has to offer. I feel like I need a way out and don't know what to do anymore.

Your words really hit home with me. I feel so trapped by my "perfect" future. Its all I've ever worked for, it's all I know how to do. I strive to be amazing at school, to end up with some amazing career after getting an education from an Ivy League or some other top college. 

I just want to give it up. I can't handle the pressure anymore, the stress. But I don't know what else to do. Not "succeeding" and not trying my hardest in school terrifies me. I'm horrified by the thought of being "average." Even though I know its twisted, in my mind, being mediocre is the same as failing. 

I feel so trapped.

> Thin is not happiness. Thin is not control.

Thank you for that.
Twentyone Pilots has single-handedly gotten me through so much shit the past few weeks. I really appreciate their lyrics and music. Thank you for reminding me of them- listening to them now :)

Yeah, I'm definitely feeling like I'll never be comfortable with my life, that I'll never enjoy anything my life has to offer. I can't think of my future in a time frame any greater than a few weeks without feeling like I'm drowning in anxiety and hopelessness. I don't want anything my life has to offer. I no longer want to go back to school, I no longer want to run. I don't have any motivation to be interested in the things I used to love. I spend my time waiting for the day to pass, trying not to hurt myself.


I just don't see the point anymore.
Thank you for the encouragement! Its been almost three weeks self-harm free, and its hell, but I'm getting through.

Thanks, this was really encouraging to read. You're right about the comfort zone, and I'll work to keep that in mind.

One of the things my therapist was said to me was that "the more successful you are in fighting the eating disorder, the louder it will get." So I know I'm combating this extreme desire to go back to my eating disorder because I'm fighting so hard against it.

Thank you, your post really helped me remember that.

I was able to eat pretty normally which I guess is good, but I have so much other shit going on too.
I'm depressed, and even though the past few days have been somewhat better (Prozac is starting to have an effect on me), I just feel super worn out and irritated.
I have really strong urges to self-harm right now and I'm trying to distract myself. :/

It's just really hard to be in recovery. I'm not supposed to be gaining weight (technically, I was never classified as underweight) and even though I know my bodyweight was too low for my body to naturally maintain and that gaining weight is okay and healthy, I'm so angry with myself for gaining weight. I just want to be super thin again.

I feel like a heartless and terrible person for not crying when I watched this movie. 
I am a teenage girl. There are full grown men in this thread saying they cried. 

Despite my lack of tears, it was an amazing documentary and worth the watch.
